item.title: Reimagining Small Business Futures - AI, Inclusion, and Territorial Innovation
item.content:encoded:
Nicola Cucari, Sapienza University of Rome

Guanglei Zhang, Wuhan University of Technology

Jintao Lu, Shanxi University of Electronic Science and Technology

Hua Fan, Shanghai International Studies University

Eric Liguori, Florida State University

The global innovation landscape is undergoing a profound restructuring. Collaboration among geographically distributed innovation ecosystems is intensifying. At the same time, the rapid advancement and diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping the dynamics of global industrial competition. New innovation hubs are emerging across the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, and several emerging economies. In parallel, digital technologies, platformization, and the decentralization of computing power are reducing traditional geographical and scale barriers. As a result, the conditions for competition and innovation are being fundamentally redefined. In this context, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are no longer structurally disadvantaged. Instead, they can increasingly act as agile and innovation-driven players within global value chains.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-driven business model innovation in SMEs
  • Digital transformation pathways under technological turbulence
  • AI and sustainable competitive advantage in resource-constrained firms
  • AI-enabled work redesign and organizational reconfiguration in SMEs
  • Inclusive AI ecosystems for minority, women, migrant, and informal entrepreneurs
  • Algorithmic Bias and transparency in AI-assisted SMEs
  • AI-enabled territorial innovation and smart regional development
  • Public policies supporting equitable AI adoption among SMEs
  • AI, cybersecurity, and risk governance in small businesses
  • Human–AI collaboration and entrepreneurial decision-making
  • Data strategies and knowledge management in SMEs
  • Data ownership and territorial digital autonomy in AI-driven SME development
  • Ethical, social, and governance implications of AI adoption
  • AI platforms and SME participation in digital value chains
  • AI for local resilience, crisis response, and adaptive entrepreneurship

item.title: SMEs: Towards New Business Models?
item.content:encoded:
Marion Polge, Université de Montpellier

Isabelle Calmé, Université de Tours

Colette Fourcade, Université de Montpellier

For a long time considered as the "small scale" of SMEs, Very Small Enterprises (SMEs) remain marginalized as an autonomous object of study in management research. Yet the foundational work of P.-A. Julien and M. Marchesnay laid essential foundations: the first by highlighting the constitutive heterogeneity of the SME population, the second by identifying the characteristics specific to the management system of the "hypofirm." This special issue follows in their footsteps, reinterrogating their contributions to SME research without, however, leading to an in-depth exploration of their most reduced segment, particularly SMEs. Beyond the size effect, can SMEs be distinguished from SMEs by their nature?

Appel publié par Revue internationale P M E Économie et gestion de la petite et moyenne entreprise. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Atypical strategic trajectories and diversification of SME leader profiles: profiles, motivations, relationship to work and risk, career bifurcations
  • Redefining performance in SMEs: alternative indicators, rejection of growth, work-life balance, territorial anchoring, relationship to living systems
  • SMEs, ecology and resource scarcity: frugal business models, circular economy, chosen degrowth, regenerative enterprise, ecological impact
  • SMEs and technologies: appropriation, marginalization or resistance to digitization, artificial intelligence, uberization or platform economy
  • Alternative forms of organization and innovation: bricolage, mutualization, cooperation, hybridization of statuses, informal or hybrid practices
  • Role of SMEs in social and territorial transitions: local resilience, inclusion dynamics, responses to systemic crises, economic justice
  • Research methodologies and epistemologies adapted to SMEs: partnership research, critical approaches, life narratives, entrepreneurial ethnography
